title: Validating a reconstructed Nino 3.4 index against the CPC published series

reconstruction.source: ERSSTv5 monthly SST on its native 2-degree grid
reconstruction.weighting: area weighted on the dataset's own grid
reconstruction.baseline: the field's own month climatology over 1991-01 to 2020-12

method_notes: The index is the area-weighted SST anomaly over 5S-5N, 170W-120W on ERSSTv5's native 2-degree grid with its own cell areas; the field is never regridded.
The anomaly removes a monthly climatology built from the same field over the stated baseline window, so each calendar month is referenced to its own 30-year mean.
The ONI criterion is applied to the 3-month centred running mean: a run of at least 5 consecutive overlapping seasons at or beyond +/-0.5 degC.
The two baseline offsets are both taken over 1950-01 to 2020-12, where the CPC 1981-2010 series ends, so they cover the identical months and can be checked against each other.

The El Nino counts from the reconstruction and from the CPC ONI differ by design: the ONI re-centres its baseline every five years and so carries no warming trend, while the reconstruction is referenced to one fixed 1991-2020 climatology.
